data.text: This is the smoking gun. `gw.lan` forwards `.lan` to dns1, but it also has **DNS rebinding protection** (`private-address: 10.0.0.0/8`). Since `nas.lan` resolves to a private address (10.20.0.50), unbound strips the answer and returns an empty NOERROR. Let me confirm this behavior and rule out other causes.

data.text: I have a complete, consistent explanation. Let me report.

data.cause: The unbound resolver on gw.lan has DNS-rebinding protection (private-address: 10.0.0.0/8) that discards answers pointing at private IPs, so queries for local names like nas.lan (10.20.0.50) come back as an empty NOERROR, which getaddrinfo reports as ENOTFOUND; this only shows when a lookup happens to be served by gw.lan rather than the primary dns1.lan, which is why it is intermittent and self-clearing.
evidence: dig @10.20.0.3 nas.lan returns 'nas.lan. 10 IN A 10.20.0.50' (NOERROR, ANSWER: 1) — the authoritative/primary server dns1.lan resolves the name correctly
dig @10.20.0.1 nas.lan returns status NOERROR with ANSWER: 0 (empty answer section, MSG SIZE 36) — gw.lan's resolver returns no address for the same name
drill nas.lan @127.0.0.1 on gw.lan also returns rcode NOERROR with ANSWER: 0, confirming the empty answer comes from gw.lan's own resolver, not a broken forwarder path

cat /var/unbound/unbound.conf on gw.lan shows 'private-address: 10.0.0.0/8' and 'private-address: 127.0.0.0/8' under a comment 'DNS rebinding protection: drop answers for public names that point at private addresses', plus a forward-zone for 'lan.' to 10.20.0.3

getent hosts nas.lan on mon.lan returns 10.20.0.50, showing resolution succeeds whenever the query is answered by dns1.lan; clients are configured with dns1 first and gw second, so only queries landing on gw hit the filter
data.recommendation: Stop applying the private-address/rebinding filter to the local zone on gw.lan's unbound. The .lan data is trusted (it is forwarded from your own authoritative server dns1.lan), so it should be exempted from the private-address filtering — e.g. declare the local zone as a trusted/local-view zone (or otherwise exclude it from the private-address check) instead of relying on harden-rebind/private-address for it. Leave the internet-facing rebinding protection in place. After reloading unbound, verify that dig @10.20.0.1 nas.lan returns 10.20.0.50 like dns1 does. (A quick interim workaround is to make clients use dns1.lan as their sole/primary resolver, but the real fix is the unbound config on gw.lan.)
data.detail: unbound private-address rebinding filter strips local .lan answers
